title: Universal Studios Hollywood entry process has changed. Here's what to expect
text:
The change aims to improve crowd flow as Southern California expects more tourists during the World Cup and LA Olympics.
The change aims to improve crowd flow as Southern California expects more tourists during the World Cup and LA Olympics. Just like many things in Hollywood, the security process at Universal Studios Hollywood has gotten a makeover.
The theme park has implemented a new security set-up, requiring theme park guests as well as customers to CityWalk to go through metal detectors. Previously, only theme park guests were subjected to security screening and bag checks.
Now there are three main security hubs, creating a large, secured perimeter around both CityWalk and Universal Studios: West Hub at the traditional entrance , Central Hub near the Jurassic Parking Structure and NBC Sports Grill & Brew, and East Hub near Margaritaville and the Curious George/E.T. parking areas.
"As the Universal Studios Hollywood destination continues to evolve, we are aligning our security protocols with other Universal destinations across the country by adding metal detection hubs adjacent to the parking structures,” a Universal Studios Hollywood spokesperson said. The change in the screening process would improve crowd flow, Universal said, as Southern California prepares for increased tourism during the 2026 FIFA World Cup and 2028 LA Olympics.
For those looking to visit Universal Cinema and CityWalk, officials recommend that they arrive a little earlier than before to get to their destinations on time.
